runs.change: eval.sh: 1 kart / 6 laps / 600 s — finished 6/6, zero penalties
runs.note: Baseline for 5-lap completion with nobody else on track. AWSIM result-summary.json: finished=true, lap_count=6, laps 39.05/37.12/37.32/37.48/37.31/37.48, penalties 0 (crash 0, wall 0, over 0). The MPC log only shows 5 laps because AWSIM ended the session on the 6th crossing. Initial pose was set correctly here (yaw 127 deg), which is the difference from the NPC runs.

runs.change: imu_gnss_poser seeds initial_pose3d with the raceline yaw — grid start fixed, then rear-ended a crawling NPC
runs.note: Same scenario that beached at the grid before the fix. Now: initial pose 'yaw from raceline' fires 11 s after the orchestrator's one-shot /set_initial_pose had already failed, EKF starts at the correct 127 deg, and the kart pulls off the grid cleanly and runs ~200 m (AWSIM wall penalties: 0, was 474 s). It then hit an NPC kart at 6.8 m/s at t=39 s and stayed jammed: AWSIM's NPC karts lap in ~185 s (6.7 km/h) and are NOT published on /v2x/vehicle_positions, so collision_guard is blind to them (0 EMERGENCY, 0 slow: cap in the whole run) and lateral avoidance is off. Passing them needs a source that sees them — this is a limit of the NPC harness, not of the grid start.

runs.change: stuck_recovery first race run: 2 NPC karts, reverse-and-rejoin enabled
runs.note: First race-scenario run with stuck_recovery. It kept the session alive where R55 had ended jammed at 0 laps, but it needed 45 recoveries and did not meet the 6-lap requirement inside 600 s. Lap times are derived, not logged: this session's 'Lap N completed' line reported cumulative time (64.8/173.2/272.2/388.5/503.3 s -- a 503 s lap is impossible in a 600 s session), so the per-lap values above are the differences between consecutive readings. No result-summary.json was kept for this run; R58 re-ran the same scenario with it saved and finished 6 laps with only 9 recoveries.

runs.change: stuck_recovery: reverse, re-aim at the raceline and drive on when jammed (new package, last in the command chain)
runs.note: The R55 scenario, re-run: race.sh with 2 NPC karts, handicap and ranking on. R55 rear-ended a crawling NPC and stayed jammed for the rest of the session at 0 laps. With stuck_recovery: AWSIM result-summary.json says finished=true, lap_count=6, final_position=1, i.e. the full 6-lap requirement inside the 600 s. 9 recoveries fired, every one of them in the same 5 m patch around (89646, 43170) where the NPC blocks; each took about 5 s (reverse ~3.5 s, then pull away) and handed control straight back. No AWSIM collision or wall penalty was recorded, and collision_guard raised 0 EMERGENCY. Laps 1-2 (106.7 / 107.3 s) are the jam; once past it laps 4-6 settle at 49.7 / 49.6 / 49.7 s, still well off the 37.9 s clear-track pace because the kart cannot pass a 6.7 km/h NPC. That gap is the lateral-avoidance problem, not a recovery failure. Lap times here are AWSIM's own: in this race session the controller's 'Lap N completed' line reported cumulative session time (110/215/275/327/377/425 s), so the parser now prefers result-summary.json.
